title: Last-copy races and pickup expiry
idea: Concurrency in a library system means two requests touching the same copy or member at once; the fix makes each check-and-change one atomic step.

analogy.text: Two people see the last loaf on a shelf and both walk over. Whoever grabs it first wins; looking is not owning.
analogy.breaks: In code, without an atomic step, both can 'grab' the same loaf.

points: Check-then-act on a copy's status lets two members borrow one copy.
An atomic replace from AVAILABLE to ON_LOAN lets exactly one caller win.
The loan limit is per member, so lock the member, not the whole library.
Pickup windows expire: a sweep passes the copy to the next waiting member.

steps.caption: Unsafe version. CP-7 is the last free copy of the title.
M-1 reads the status and sees it is free.
M-2 reads too, before M-1 writes. It also sees free.
M-1 writes ON_LOAN and opens a loan.
M-2 acts on its old answer and overwrites. One copy, two loans.
Safe version. Both threads call `replace` with the expected old value.
The map applies one call at a time for this key. Whichever runs first, here M-1, matches and writes.
M-2's call expects AVAILABLE but finds ON_LOAN, so it returns false.

code.title: Prove the race
code.caption: A barrier makes both threads look before either writes, so the bug shows on every run, not by luck.

walk.text: Run the copy race unsafe, then atomic, then the member-limit case.
Safe: `replace(key, old, new)` succeeds only if the value is still AVAILABLE.
Unsafe: read, wait for the other thread, then both write and both count a loan.
A member with four loans borrows twice at once under a limit of five.
Join both threads before reading results, so the output never depends on timing.
`synchronized` makes the limit check and the increment one step per member.

code.title: Edge cases on the hold shelf
code.caption: Missed pickups, a late pickup, a double scan and a cancel. Dates are passed in, so every run prints the same.

walk.text: Two members wait; the returned copy goes to M-2 for three days.
Last pickup day kept; next day the sweep moves to M-3 and refuses M-2's late pickup.
A second scan of the same copy is ignored; M-3 then cancels.
Return is idempotent: only a copy that is ON_LOAN can be returned.
Pickup checks both the member and the deadline under the same lock as the sweep.
One method hands the copy on: next member with a deadline, or back to AVAILABLE.

pitfalls: Do not read status, then write it later; use one atomic compare-and-set.
Run the pickup sweep and the pickup under one lock, or both can win.
Treat a second return scan as a no-op; never charge the fine twice.

quiz.q: What is the first line LastCopyRace prints?
options: It changes from run to run
quiz.why: The barrier lets both threads read AVAILABLE before either writes. Both then write and both count a loan: 2.

takeaway: Looking is not owning: make check and change one atomic step.

starters: Why not lock the whole LibraryService with one big lock?
How does this change when two servers share one database?
What should happen if a pickup and the sweep run at the same moment?
